title: Irish tax on an Irish fund's distributions
answer: Irish Revenue's manual says no exit tax is deducted on transactions in units held in a recognised clearing system, such as ETFs, nor on payments to a non-resident who gave the fund a non-resident declaration, so an Irish ETF's distribution reaches an Israeli resident without Irish tax and the treaty does not change it (TXF-28).

source.title: Irish Revenue, Tax and Duty Manual Part 27-01a-02, Investment Undertakings (last updated January 2026)
source.quote: any transaction in relation to, or in respect of, units which are held in a recognised clearing system does not require the deduction of exit tax

title: Age 60+ lower brackets on withheld gains
answer: Yes, an individual's real gain, exempt-fund units included, is taxed at the s.121 rates up to 25% (s.91(ב)(1), s.91(ב1)(1ב)), so the 60+ brackets apply; the bank withholds 25% and the excess comes back through a return or form 0135, or is cut in advance by the assessing officer's written coordination under reg. 11 of the 2002 withholding regulations (TXS-23, TXS-09, TXG-25).

title: Fund-level rate in a taxable shekel fund
answer: The Tax Authority's circular 7/2003 (s.2.1.1) says a taxable fund pays the rates an individual not in business would pay, and today an individual pays 15% on unlinked interest and at most 15% of the whole gain on unlinked bonds (s.125ג(ג)(1), s.91(ב)(3)(א)) (TXS-11).
